clue.text: Easy to manage stealing note from abode

indicators.note: stealing something from a place takes it away, so these letters are removed from the home word

parts.note: an abode is a domicile, a place of residence
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone who is easily handled pinches a banknote from a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like money, but it is the sol-fa note MI, taken out of DOMICILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile animal or person is compliant and readily controlled, which is exactly being easy to manage.

clue.text: 'Bottle' stars Moore and Travolta

parts.note: the film star Demi Moore
the film star John Travolta

explanation.surface: A film title, 'Bottle', starring two Hollywood names.
explanation.walkthrough: The first names of the two stars are joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large narrow-necked glass vessel, often wicker-cased, used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: Irish County's team opener

parts.note: Cork is a county in the Republic of Ireland, with the 's adding S
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: A sports report about the side that opened the scoring for an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' reads as a first goal or batsman; it is a tool that opens wine bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the device that pulls corks from bottles, so it is a bottle opener.

clue.text: Python discovered in sediment

indicators.note: dis-covered: the cover, the outside letters, is taken off the comedian's name

parts.note: John Cleese was a member of the Monty Python comedy team

explanation.surface: A snake turns up buried in the silt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Python' looks like a snake; it is the Monty Python comic CLEESE, whose first and last letters are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs that settle at the bottom of a wine cask or bottle.

clue.text: Posh stuff husband put into pitchers

indicators.note: the husband's letter is placed inside the word for people who pitch tents

parts.note: campers are people who pitch tents

explanation.surface: A man pours something fancy into jugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitchers' suggests jugs; it means those who pitch tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is a jokey upper-class British slang word for champagne, the sparkling wine of smart occasions.

clue.text: Bacchanalian party held by female in charge

indicators.note: the party word sits inside the female word, held by it

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A wild party is hosted by the woman running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonic means devoted to pleasure, which fits the drunken revelry associated with Bacchus, god of wine.

clue.text: Contractor stores one key grape

indicators.note: the contracting tissue keeps the other letters inside it, as goods held in store

parts.note: a muscle is something that contracts
a means one
Del (Delete) is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A building contractor keeps a crucial variety of grape in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' suggests a builder; it is a muscle, which contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadelle is a white wine grape variety grown chiefly in Bordeaux and Australia.

clue.text: Praise old sailor having had tip-off?

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: the tip, the first letter, of the seaman word comes off

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A retired seaman is commended after receiving a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-off' reads as a warning; here it removes the first letter, the tip, of SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to glorify or extol them, synonyms for praising them highly.

clue.text: Wander into quiet yard — it's fortified

indicators.note: the straying word goes inside the letters for quiet and yard

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to err is to stray or wander

explanation.surface: Someone strays into a silent courtyard of a stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine, strengthened with added brandy, from around Jerez in Spain.

clue.text: Somewhat better alcohol to be served up

definitions.text: Somewhat better alcohol to be served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters run upwards, read backwards
only some of the two words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A claim that a finer wine is to be offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a description of the red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret, the red wine of Bordeaux, is a rather better alcoholic drink to serve at table.

clue.text: Comic publisher left, editor was amazed

parts.note: Marvel is the publisher of Spider-Man and other comic books

explanation.surface: A comics firm's editor walked out, and was astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: To marvel is to wonder at something, so the past tense means was astonished.

clue.text: Verona's drop of espresso average

indicators.note: the answer is made of part of the next two words, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: An Italian café verdict on a middling shot of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop of espresso' looks like a unit; 'drop' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the hills east of Verona, so it is a local drop.

clue.text: Succeeded in project by a whisker

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for stick out

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A scheme pulled through with almost no margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adverb means only barely or narrowly, the same as by a whisker.

clue.text: Player who's perhaps switched sides gets negotiator

parts.note: trans- is a prefix meaning across or over to the other side
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A sportsman who changed teams goes into contract talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'switched sides' suggest a footballer transferring clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A transactor is someone who carries out deals or business, conducting the dealing between parties.

clue.text: Expert one got Lois in a state

indicators.note: something in a state is disordered and agitated, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A specialist reduced a woman named Lois to a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' suggests a US state or a country; it signals the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenologist is a scientific specialist in wine and winemaking, an authority on the subject.

clue.text: Gathering hears TV broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A meeting listens to a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suits TV, but originally meant scattering seed, linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The harvest is the gathering in of a crop, especially grapes for wine.

clue.text: Briefly applaud south-east Cheshire maybe

indicators.note: said briefly, the clapping word loses its last letter

parts.note: to cheer is to applaud

explanation.surface: A quick round of applause for a place in south-eastern Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county, but also a crumbly English cheese named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is one example of a cheese, hence 'maybe' marking it as one of many varieties.

clue.text: Waiter weaving more lies around top of menu

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the menu's first letter
weaving interlaces strands, so these letters are moved over and under each other
the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant server spins untruths about the dishes on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' jumbles MORE LIES into SOMELIER, set 'around' the M from 'top of menu'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine waiter, the restaurant employee who advises on and serves the wine.

clue.text: Ultimate decider of a police departmental match?

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Asking what finally settles a contest between police departments.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid test is a conclusive trial, originally of gold with nitric acid, that settles a question.

clue.text: Sorry after empty show nosedives

indicators.note: the apology comes after the emptied word
with its contents removed only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: oops is a word of apology for a blunder

explanation.surface: An apology follows a hollow performance that flops.
explanation.definitionFit: Swoops are sudden rushing descents through the air, like a bird diving.

clue.text: Elvish folk spin in places

indicators.note: the spin letters go inside the word for locations

parts.note: sites are places or locations
PR, public relations, is spin

explanation.surface: Fairy creatures twirl about at various spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' looks like a whirling movement; it is media spin, public relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are elves or fairies, small supernatural beings of folklore.

clue.text: Staff getting bug possibly creates controversy

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod
a bug can be a hidden microphone, a mic

explanation.surface: A worker catching an insect causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a fierce written or spoken attack, so it is a piece of controversy.

clue.text: Ignore ticket on unoccupied Bentley

parts.note: a pass is a ticket giving admission

indicators.note: with no occupants only the outer letters of the car name remain

explanation.surface: Disregard the parking fine stuck on an empty luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass by something is to disregard it, overlooking it without stopping.

clue.text: Transfer cycling Geordie duo on the box

indicators.note: cycling turns the letters round, moving a run from the front to the back

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a TV presenting pair from Newcastle, whose natives are called Geordies

explanation.surface: Two Newcastle TV presenters move house while out on their bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT DEC becomes DEC ANT when cycled.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant wine is to transfer it from bottle to another vessel, leaving sediment behind.

clue.text: Cruise too choppy near Malta for whale spotting?

indicators.note: the Malta letter is placed next to the jumbled letters
choppy water is rough and broken up, so these letters are tossed about

parts.note: M is the international vehicle code for Malta

explanation.surface: A rough sea cruise off Malta for whale watchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecotourism is travel to view nature and wildlife; whale watching is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sheepish bearer of grapes bearing nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue the vine word carries the zero on top of it

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a vine is the plant that bears grapes

explanation.surface: A shamefaced grapevine that has produced no fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' reads as embarrassed, but means of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means relating to or resembling sheep, the literal sense of sheepish.

clue.text: Mother recalled swallowing energy drink

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the energy letter inside it
called back, so the word for a mother animal is read backwards

parts.note: a dam is a mother, of animals
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Mum, remembering, gulps down a sports drink.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM, reversed to MAD, swallows E.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink made by fermenting honey and water.

clue.text: Paddington's home page initially enrages rail union

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A home page that angers a railway trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London railway station but also the bear from darkest Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear, the children's book character, came to London from Peru.

clue.text: Bimbo regularly interrupts boxer's defence

indicators.note: the picked letters break into the boxer's name

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxer

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A floozy keeps cutting in on a fighter's guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' looks like a boxer's guard; it is a legal defence.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea that one was elsewhere when a crime happened, a defence in law.

clue.text: Ordered new balti and eastern booze

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so these letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone ordered a new balti curry and Asian drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as asked for in a restaurant; it signals rearranging. A balti is a curry served in British Indian restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Table wine is ordinary wine for drinking with meals, so it is booze.

clue.text: Free entertainment is essentially cheap work

parts.note: a treat is entertainment paid for by someone else

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letter

explanation.surface: Getting a show for nothing is basically a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' reads as labour; here it is a written work.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a written work dealing formally and methodically with a subject.

clue.text: In Rhineland, it's good red plonk

parts.note: gut is German for good, as 'In Rhineland' says
rot is German for red

explanation.surface: A German says this red wine is a fine one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rhineland' tells you to use German words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutrot is cheap, nasty alcohol, the same idea as plonk, poor-quality wine.
